steps.note: S1.2.1 states the net target change (JV+RG)x independent of the initial side/central values a, c because rows 0-1 subtract, the middle rows add, and rows 6-7 restore c, a.
S1.2.2 gives central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, side wires cancelling exactly the intersection-one cases, zero/two intersections already zero, and self coefficient one.
S1.2.3 gives central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2, side cancellation for intersections zero and two, intersection one contributing zero, self coefficient one.
S1.2.4 gives the three stages (x,y) -> (x,y+x) -> (-y,y+x) -> (-y,x), and S1.2/S1.2.1 state that each invocation restores its scratch wires.
The plan says only that an edge's rank change is the dimension of its residual and that edges join comparable labels (S1.4.1.5); the per-edge residual table with its dimensions is never stated.
S1.4.1.4 has the inclusion P(x)<t_X> inside P(x)t_Y-perp because t_X is orthogonal to t_Y, but never the complement <t_X,t_Y>-perp or its dimension h-2, so the residual of edge 2->5 is not derived.
Plan states center 3->4 as the only decreasing edge losing h, sources N and sinks Wm-N, signed total Wm-2N by telescoping at gates, and absolute total Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich.
S1.4.1.7b states each nonzero residual over F2 is nondegenerate with a norm-one unit (nonalternating), hence an orthonormal basis, with alternating planes absorbed via w+a, w+b, w+a+b.
S1.4.1.7c states L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2.

S1.4.1.9.2 gives wt(z+w) with even intersection for orthogonal vectors hence additivity mod 4, and S1.4.1.9 plus 9.3 decompose the phase difference over an orthonormal residual basis with coefficient wt(v) per vector (the sum formula is not written out literally).
S1.4.1.9.3 gives wt(v) odd, phase i^(eps[v.x]) = (1+i^eps)/2 + (1-i^eps)/2 (-1)^(v.x), and H diag(1,-1) H = X turning it into the kernel aI+bX_v or its inverse.

Stated in its layer form: one factor (C^eps)^(tensor f) on the f columns per residual vector (S1.4.4.1.4), s_c such factors over the network (S1.4.4.1.7); the general k-column identity is not written separately, so this is a borderline credit.

Plan has both deficits exceeding 20*2^-50, log m<20, m^(1-2^-50) > m(1-20*2^-50) > m(1-eta), and s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^-50.

S1.4.3.1.2 gives the elimination (topmost nonzero row, rightmost pivot, lower-triangular column and row clearing, delete row and column and repeat, one rank-one block per step) and S1.4.3.1.1 gives Pi with exactly a ones.
S1.4.3.1.3 names a prime q avoiding all denominators and diagonal numerators; the finite table and the specialization to Z/q^b are not spelled out, so this is a thin credit.
